headline: Ratchet & Clank's source gets clearer names, shared structures and more C data
summary: Work focused on making the original game's recovered source easier to read and maintain: shared structures replace private copies, and names replace numeric buttons, levels and player states. More data and pointer blocks moved into C, alongside checks for questionable matching techniques. The snapshot still records all 5116 functions and 100% of code by size as matched, meaning they compile to exactly the original game's bytes.
highlights: Button names replace 967 input masks, level names replace 474 numbers, and player state names replace 7249 numbers (#188, #189, #190).
Three batches move data and pointer blocks into C (#196, #197, #198).
A scanner flags 118 suspect sites, and 48 unnecessary volatile and register workarounds were removed (#194, #195).
